history.dynasty: Goud Saraswat Brahmin community; relocated under Portuguese persecution
history.summary: The original Ramnathi temple stood at Loutolim in Salcete. During the Portuguese temple-destruction campaign of the 16th century, the Mahajans migrated with their deities to Bandora in the Antruz Mahal region (then under the Bijapur Sultanate) in 1566, where five separate temples were built for the Panchayatana deities. In May 2011 the temple completed 450 years at its present location. The complex was largely rebuilt in 1905. Tradition: Ramnath is a Shaivite deity ('Ram-Nath' = Lord of Rama); legend says Rama installed a Shivalinga at Rameshwar to absolve the sin of killing Ravana. The temple is the kuladev of Goud Saraswat Brahmins (Shenvi/Shenai), Daivadnya Brahmins and Vaishyas of the Gokarn and Kashi Maths. CSV town correction: the temple is at Ramnathim, Bandora, Ponda (North Goa), NOT Panaji as the CSV claims.

name: Shree Ramnath Temple
town_description: Ramnathim (Bandora) is a village in Ponda taluka, North Goa, about 30 km from Panaji, in the temple belt of the former Antruz Mahal where many Salcete temples were relocated during the 16th-century Portuguese persecutions.
